sentences.text: With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, this Criminal Appeal is heard finally.

2. Appellant is aggrieved of the judgment dated 25.09.2023 passed by learned Special Judge (POCSO Act, 2012) and 18th Addl. Sessions Judge, Jabalpur District Jabalpur in Special Case No.
165 of 2022, whereby the learned trial Court has convicted and sentenced the appellant under Sections 3 read with Section 4(2) of POCSO Act, 2012 with rigorous imprisonment for 20 years and fine of Rs.2000/- with default stipulations of rigorous imprisonment of one year.

entities.text: 18th Addl. Sessions Judge, Jabalpur District Jabalpur

sentences.text: It is pointed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55344 2 CRA-12646-2023 out that, appellant has also been convicted under Section 376(3) and 376(2)(N) IPC but sentence has been given under Section 3 read with Section 4(2) of POCSO, Act, 2012.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that, facts of the present case in short are that, on 01.08.2022, mother of the victim lodged a report at Police Station Adhartal, District Jabalpur informing that victim had gone missing.
This report is available on record as Ex.P-4, on the basis of which FIR (Ex.P-5) was recorded registering Case Crime No. 772 of 2022 under Section 363 IPC.

sentences.text: It was alleged that, when the parents and family members of the victim were sleeping, at about 06:00 a.m. on 01.08.2022 victim left her home without informing anybody.
During the investigation, Investigating Officer of the case had recorded statements of the witnesses.

On 26.08.2022 victim was recovered vide recovery Panchnama (Ex.P-1) and with the permission of the mother of the victim as contained in Ex.P-6 she was subjected to medical examination at Elgin Hospital, Jabalpur.
Her examination report is Ex.P-15A.
Her vaginal slide etc. were seized and seizure memo Ex.P-15 was prepared.
5. Thereafter, appellant was arrested on the same day.
His blood sample and semen sample etc. were drawn.
Statements of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. were recorded as contained in Ex.P-2 and Ex.P-8, thereafter, samples were subjected to DNA examination.

DNA report is Ex.P-20 which makes a mention that, there is uninterpretable NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55344 3 CRA-12646-2023 low Y Profile obtained from the vaginal slide of the victim and therefore, did not give any definite opinion.
6. It is submitted that, it will be evident from the statements of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. as contained in Ex.P-2 that she was a consenting party and therefore, it is submitted that, since victim has admitted that she had travelled to the house of Paras Choudhary on her own volition and was neither under any force and coercion to travel with him, and has further stated that she was in love relationship with the appellant, it is a fit case for acquittal of the appellant.
7.

It is also submitted that, about 1 years back, appellant performed marriage with the victim and thereafter, there is nobody to take care of the victim and she is in fact facing double crusade of unequal treatment in as much as she being not looked after by anybody and at the same time her husband is in custody.
8.
It is further submitted that, PW-2 (mother of the victim) has stated that she is not interested in keeping the victim.

It is also pointed out that the child born out of the relationship is now aged about 1 years and therefore, it is prayed that these special circumstances should be taken into considerations impugned judgment of conviction be set aside.
9. Shri Rajeev Gupta, learned counsel for the objector supports the case of the appellant and submits that, he be acquitted from the charges.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55344 4 CRA-12646-2023 10.
Shri Nitin Gupta, learned Government Advocate for the State, in his turn submits that, the age of the victim is important.
As per Radiologist report contained in Ex.P-12, age of the victim is shown to be between 15 to 17 years and therefore, she being a minor cannot be treated to be a consenting party.

11. At this stage, Shri Hanmant Rao Naidu, learned counsel for the appellant places reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of K. Dandapani Vs. The State by the Inspector of Police [Criminal Appeal No. 796 of 2022 {Arising out of Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No. 9698 of Parash Choudhary vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92408512/
2 2019}

12. Reliance is also placed on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of K. Kirubakaran Vs. State of Tamil Nadu (Criminal Appeal No. 679 of 2024) decided on 28.10.2025, wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court, invoked its power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India to quash the criminal proceedings against the appellant including the conviction and sentence.

sentences.text: 13. After hearing, learned counsel for the parties and going through the records.

14. In the backdrop of the factual background mentioned above, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55344 5 CRA-12646-2023 on 29.10.2022, learned trial Court had framed charges against the appellant under Section 363, 366, 376(3) & 376(2)(N) of IPC.
Charges were also framed under Section 3 read with Section 4 so also under Section 5(L) read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012.

15. It is true that, victim while giving her statements before the Judicial Magistrate as contained in Ex.P-2 mentioned that, on 01.08.2022 at about 05:00 a.m. she had travelled to Gadarwara in a train.
From Gadarwara she had called Paras threatening him to take her, then Paras came to the Station and took her to the village of his sister.
She resided at the house of sister of Paras for 20-25 days.
Paras was also residing there.
Victim was residing with the sister of the appellant as appellant used to go to attend work.
Thereafter, she has stated that, physical relationship was established with her consent.
Paras had not used any force or coercion.
Then, she has stated that, she had gone to the house of the sister of Paras on her own volition because she is in love with Paras.
Subsequently she stated that, she wants to live with Paras.
16. Ex.P-3 is the progress report of the victim showing her date of birth to be 23.09.2007.

This fact is not disputed in the backdrop of Dakhilkharij Register (Ex.P-9) in which the name of the victim is mentioned at Sl. No.9 showing her date of birth to be 23.09.2007 proved by the School Teacher (PW-3).
Medical Examination Report of the victim is Ex.P-15.
She was examined by Dr. Swati Nema (PW-8).
In the Medical Examination Report, it is mentioned that, her secondary sexual NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55344 6 CRA-12646-2023 characteristics were well developed.
Her menses was on since age of 14 years, LMP 5/8/22, history of last sexual intercourse was on 23.08.2022.
Upon General examination, there were no signs of external or internal injury.
Vaginal smear slides were prepared and handed over to the Police and Doctor stated that no definite opinion can be given about the sexual intercourse.

It is also mentioned in the MLC report Ex.P-15 that Doctor had advised X-ray for age determination beside UPT.
17.
X-ray report is available on record as Ex.P-12 showing her age to be between 15 to 17 years.
FSL Report is Ex.P-19 which says that on Ex.A Slide of the victim and on Ex.B Slide obtained from the accused there were human sperm.

However, DNA/Finger Printing Report (Ex.P- Parash Choudhary vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92408512/
3 20) reveals that the profile as obtained from vaginal slide (Ex.A) was so uninterpretable low that its further testing is not possible.

sentences.text:
18. We have gone through the evidence of victim (PW-1) who has almost remained consistent and has deposed on the same line as she had given her statement before the learned Magistrate under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
19.
Mother of the victim (PW-2) stated that, her current age is 37 years which she has stated on estimation.
Her marriage was performed 21 years back.
Then she stated that, for last 19 years, she is residing in her in-laws house alongwith her husband.
She has further stated that, after one year of her marriage, a child had come in her womb but that was aborted.
Five months thereafter, another girl had come in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55344 7 CRA-12646-2023 her womb and thereafter, victim is born.
She further stated that her husband died about 04 years back and she is taking care of both of her children.
20. Thus, as per the chronology given by the mother of the victim (PW-2), it is evident that, victim was minor at the time of the incident.
This evidence of PW-2 (mother of the victim) as narrated in para-6 of her cross-examination corroborates the medical age of the victim as given by the Radiologist in Ex.P-12.
21. Manisha Thakur (PW-3), Principal of the School at Jabalpur has proved the date of birth of the victim to be 23.09.2007.

Dr. Manish Mishra (PW-4), Radiologist at Victoria Hospital, Jabalpur which is a Government Hospital was examined and he has categorically stated in his cross-examination that age of victim was not above 18 years.
22. Dr. Swati Nema (PW-8) is the lady Doctor who had referred the patient for age determination.

Thus, when all these facts are cumulatively taken into consideration, then, there is a medical evidence corroborated with school record to show that victim was not a major.
23.

When, in this back drop, judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court are taken into consideration,
then in the case of K. Dandapani (Supra), Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that, "In the peculiar facts of the case and shall not be treated as a precedent".
Thus, it is evident that, Hon'ble Supreme Court was exercising its authority under Article 142 of the Constitution of India which is not vested in the High Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55344 8 CRA-12646-2023 24.

In the case of K. Kirubakaran (supra), Hon'ble Supreme Court has categorically mentioned in para-11 of the judgment that " we deem it appropriate to invoke our powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India to quash the criminal proceedings against the appellant including the conviction and sentence".

In the case of Re:
Right to Privacy of Adolescents in Suo Motu Writ Petition (C) No. 3 of 2023 with Criminal Appeal No. 1451 of 2024 decided on 23.05.2025 reported in 2025 SCC Parash Choudhary vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92408512/
4 OnLine SC 1200, Hon'ble Supreme Court in para 31 (a) has has noted that "We exercise our extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of India and hold that though the accused stands convicted, he will not undergo sentence for the reasons stated earlier";
25.

entities.text: SCC Parash Choudhary vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, these three judgments in hand i.e. the case of K.Dandapani (supra), K. Kirubakaran (supra) and In Re: Right to Privacy of Adolescents (supra) , we are not left with any option but to hold that since victim was admittedly a minor, and this High Court has no powers akin to Article 142 of the Constitution of India and law being well settled that there can not be any consent of a minor,
we are constrained to observe that impugned judgment of conviction cannot be interfered with at our level and there is no illegality or irregularity in the appreciation of evidence or passing of the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence.
26.
Accordingly, appeal fails and is dismissed.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55344 9 CRA-12646-2023 27.
The case property be disposed off in terms of the judgment of the trial Court.
Record of the trial Court be sent back.
Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) (AVANINDRA KUMA  JUDGE JUDGE  AR Parash Choudhary vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92408512/
